platform: Mastodon and Mastodon-API-compatible servers (Pleroma/Akkoma, GoToSocial, Friendica, Pixelfed, Mitra, Iceshrimp.NET)

official_api.name: Mastodon REST API (per-instance; dynamic client registration via POST /api/v1/apps)
official_api.auth: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code per instance. Flow: (1) POST https://{instance}/api/v1/apps (no auth) with client_name, redirect_uris (String or, on Mastodon 4.3+, Array of Strings; use a newline-separated single string for widest compatibility - Pixelfed explodes on \n and Mitra's spec types it as string), scopes (space-separated, default 'read'), website -> {client_id, client_secret, client_secret_expires_at (0 = never), redirect_uris[], id, name, website, scopes[]}; vapid_key deprecated 4.3. (2) Open https://{instance}/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=..&redirect_uri=..&scope=write:statuses%20write:media%20profile&state=..&code_challenge=..&code_challenge_method=S256 (PKCE S256 accepted since 4.3.0, optional today, planned mandatory in 5.0; force_login=true and lang=xx optional). (3) POST https://{instance}/oauth/token form: grant_type=authorization_code, code, client_id, client_secret (REQUIRED - Mastodon only supports confidential clients today, Doorkeeper 5.9.9; public-client PR #30329 is still a draft), redirect_uri (must equal one registered), code_verifier (if PKCE) -> {access_token, token_type:'Bearer', scope, created_at}. Discovery: GET https://{instance}/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server (RFC 8414, 4.3+). Revoke: POST /oauth/revoke (client_id, client_secret, token). Verify: GET /api/v1/accounts/verify_credentials (needs 'profile' or read:accounts). redirect_uri rules (verified in Doorkeeper lib/doorkeeper/oauth/helpers/uri_checker.rb 5.9.9 + Mastodon config/initializers/doorkeeper.rb): exact string match except that for loopback hosts (127.0.0.1, ::1, localhost) the PORT is ignored per RFC 8252 7.3 - so register http://127.0.0.1/callback and use http://127.0.0.1:{ephemeral}/callback; force_ssl_in_redirect_uri is false so plain http loopback is accepted; custom schemes (neforum://callback) are accepted (only data:/javascript:/vbscript: schemes and a literal 'localhost' scheme are rejected); query string must match exactly; fragments are rejected; urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob is still supported (not deprecated as of 4.4 docs) and shows the code on a page for manual copy. Old 'password' grant removed in 4.4.
oauth_scopes: write (umbrella; required on Pixelfed because it checks tokenCan('write'))
read:statuses (only if you list/cancel scheduled posts)

endpoints.request_shape: form/json: client_name (req), redirect_uris (req; string with \n separators or array on 4.3+), scopes='write:statuses write:media profile', website
endpoints.response_shape: {id, name, website, scopes[], redirect_uris[], redirect_uri (deprecated), client_id, client_secret, client_secret_expires_at:0}
endpoints.notes: Rate-limited 5 per 10 min per IP (rack_attack throttle_oauth_application_registrations/ip, added 4.3 when app vacuuming was removed). Pixelfed returns 404 if OAUTH_ENABLED=false and returns singular redirect_uri (comma-joined) + vapid_key:null.

endpoints.request_shape: query: response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, scope, state, code_challenge, code_challenge_method=S256, force_login, lang
endpoints.response_shape: 302 to redirect_uri?code=..&state=.. (or code shown on-page for oob)
endpoints.notes: Open in system browser (ASWebAuthenticationSession / Custom Tabs / default browser), not a WebView.

endpoints.request_shape: form: grant_type=authorization_code, code, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, code_verifier, (scope)
endpoints.notes: Token never expires (Doorkeeper access_token_expires_in nil), no refresh_token. GoToSocial same (AccessTokenExp 0). Pleroma/Akkoma additionally support grant_type=refresh_token and password.

endpoints.response_shape: configuration.statuses.{max_characters, max_media_attachments, characters_reserved_per_url}; configuration.media_attachments.{supported_mime_types[], image_size_limit, image_matrix_limit, video_size_limit, video_frame_rate_limit, video_matrix_limit, description_limit (4.4+)}; configuration.polls.{max_options, max_characters_per_option, min_expiration, max_expiration}; api_versions {mastodon: N} (4.3+); version string
endpoints.notes: Fall back to GET /api/v1/instance (Pleroma/Akkoma expose max_toot_chars, upload_limit, poll_limits, max_media_attachments there). Pixelfed reports polls all 0, image/video size = max_photo_size*1024, matrix 2073600.

endpoints.request_shape: multipart/form-data: file (req, include a filename), description (alt text), focus='x,y' (-1.0..1.0), thumbnail
endpoints.response_shape: 200 {MediaAttachment with url} when processed synchronously (images); 202 {MediaAttachment with url:null} when queued (video/gifv/audio); 401; 422 unsupported file type; 500 thumbnail/processing failure
endpoints.notes: Then poll GET /api/v1/media/:id until 200 (206 Partial Content = still processing; 422 = failed). Posting with an unprocessed id -> 422 'Cannot attach files that have not finished processing'. Scope write:media. Pixelfed always answers 202. POST /api/v1/media (sync) deprecated since 3.1.3 but still works.

endpoints.purpose: Update alt text / focus before posting
endpoints.notes: Only before the attachment is used in a status.

endpoints.request_shape: form or JSON: status (req unless media_ids), media_ids[] (max max_media_attachments; cannot combine with poll), poll[options][] + poll[expires_in] (seconds; poll[multiple], poll[hide_totals]), in_reply_to_id, sensitive (bool), spoiler_text, visibility in public|unlisted|private|direct, language (ISO 639-1), scheduled_at (ISO 8601/RFC 3339, >= 5 minutes in the future), quoted_status_id + quote_approval_policy (4.5+). Headers: Authorization: Bearer, Idempotency-Key: <uuid>
endpoints.response_shape: 200 Status entity; or 200 ScheduledStatus {id, scheduled_at, params{text, media_ids, ...}, media_attachments[]} when scheduled_at is set; 401; 422 'Validation failed: ...' (text blank, too long, media not ready, images+video mixed); 429
endpoints.notes: Idempotency: key stored in Redis 1 h per account; a replay returns the ORIGINAL Status (200), not an error (PostStatusService rescues IdempotencyError and returns e.status). Scheduling limits: 300 total, 25 per day (ScheduledStatus::TOTAL_LIMIT/DAILY_LIMIT). Scope write:statuses. Server does the scheduling itself - no client timer needed.

endpoints.url: https://{instance}/api/v1/scheduled_statuses (GET list, read:statuses; GET /:id; PUT /:id form scheduled_at, write:statuses; DELETE /:id, write:statuses)

official_api.free_tier: Entire API is free on every instance; no developer account, no app review. Only cost is the user's own account on that instance. (Valid 2026-10-07.)
official_api.rate_limits: Mastodon (docs + rack_attack.rb, main): 300 requests / 5 min per access token (throttle_per_token_api), 1500 / 5 min per authenticated user, 300 / 5 min per IP unauthenticated; POST media 30 / 30 min; DELETE statuses 30 / 30 min; POST /api/v1/apps 5 / 10 min per IP; headers X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset (ISO 8601); 429 JSON on exceed, no Retry-After. GoToSocial: 300 / 5 min PER CLIENT IP (not per token) across the whole API, 429 + same headers. Pixelfed: 1000 posts / 24 h per user (429), 1250 media uploads / day. Per-account limits also apply: 300 scheduled posts total, 25 scheduled per day.
official_api.app_review_required: None. Register per instance at runtime via POST /api/v1/apps; nothing to audit.
official_api.unreviewed_app_restrictions: None - every dynamically-registered app has full access to the scopes the user approves. Instance admins can still revoke apps and some instances rate-limit or block app registration by IP.
official_api.account_requirements: Any normal user account on the instance; no business/creator/professional tier exists. Pixelfed instances must have OAUTH_ENABLED=true (default true) or /api/v1/apps 404s.
official_api.media_upload_flow: 1) GET /api/v2/instance -> read supported_mime_types, image_size_limit (default 16 MiB), video_size_limit (default 99 MiB), image_matrix_limit (33,177,600 px; GIFs 921,600 px = 1280x720), video_matrix_limit (8,294,400 px = 3840x2160, max 120 fps, max 36,000 frames), max_media_attachments (4), description_limit. 2) For each file POST /api/v2/media multipart (file + description + focus) with Bearer token (write:media). 3) If 202, poll GET /api/v1/media/:id every ~1-2 s until 200 (206 = processing, 422 = failed). 4) POST /api/v1/statuses with media_ids[] in display order. Rules: images cannot be mixed with a video or audio file ('Images and video cannot be attached together'); a status can have media OR a poll, not both; Mastodon processes images synchronously (200) and video/gifv/audio asynchronously (202). Media ids must belong to the same account and be unused. Default MIME types: image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, image/webp; video/webm, video/mp4, video/quicktime, video/ogg; audio wav/ogg/mp3/flac/aac/m4a/mp4/3gpp/webm/asf. Pixelfed default media_types is image/jpeg,image/jpg,image/png,image/gif only (admin may add video/mp4); max_photo_size default 15000 KB; alt text max 1000.
official_api.server_side_scheduling: Yes - pass scheduled_at (>= 5 min ahead) to POST /api/v1/statuses; server returns a ScheduledStatus and publishes it itself. Limits 300 total / 25 per day. Supported by Mastodon (2.7+), GoToSocial (added Aug 2025, same 300/25 limits documented in its statuses config), Friendica (create only; no PUT reschedule). NOT supported by Pixelfed (parameter ignored/absent). Pleroma/Akkoma: scheduled_statuses endpoints exist in Pleroma's Mastodon-API implementation but not re-verified here. Mitra: not in its OpenAPI spec.
official_api.token_lifetime_and_refresh: Mastodon access tokens never expire (config/initializers/doorkeeper.rb: access_token_expires_in nil, use_refresh_token off, reuse_access_token on); no refresh_token is issued. Tokens die only when the user revokes the app, the app is deleted, or POST /oauth/revoke. Planned (PR #30329 draft, FediForum 2025-06 session): optional 'offline_access' scope with refresh tokens and short-lived tokens for public clients, plus revocation of tokens unused for 2 years, targeted at Mastodon 5.0 - so store tokens but be ready to re-auth on 401. GoToSocial: same, never expires, no refresh. Pleroma/Akkoma: tokens can expire and grant_type=refresh_token is supported.

handoff.web_intent_params: text=<urlencoded text>; also title=<...> and url=<...>; optional visibility=public|unlisted|private|direct. Server (app/helpers/application_helper.rb render_initial_state) builds the composer text as [title, text, url].compact.join(' ') (space-joined, in that order); visibility is honoured only if it is MORE private than the user's default. Requires the user to be logged in on that instance (SharesController before_action :authenticate_user!) - unauthenticated users get the login page then return. No media can be prefilled. The instance's PWA manifest share_target is GET share?title={title}&text={text}&url={url} (no files). The user must still press Publish. Non-Mastodon servers: GoToSocial has no /share; Pixelfed/Akkoma/Friendica have their own web UIs (no verified /share equivalent).
handoff.android_share: Official app package org.joinmastodon.android (F-Droid/Play). Activity org.joinmastodon.android.ExternalShareActivity declares intent-filters for android.intent.action.SEND and SEND_MULTIPLE with mimeType */*; it reads Intent.EXTRA_TEXT, EXTRA_SUBJECT, EXTRA_STREAM (single) or ClipData (multiple) without MIME filtering and opens the composer with prefilledText and mediaAttachments. It also handles the deep link mastodon://share?text=<urlencoded> (text only). Third-party clients (Tusky, Fedilab, Moshidon, etc.) register their own ACTION_SEND filters, so the generic Android share sheet (no package pinned) is the most robust hand-off; pin the package only if the user chose the official app.
handoff.ios_share: Official app (mastodon/mastodon-ios) ships a Share Extension target 'ShareActionExtension' (NSExtensionPointIdentifier com.apple.share-services) whose activation rule accepts text, 1 web URL, up to 4 images and 1 movie - so UIActivityViewController with text + images reaches the composer. The app registers the URL scheme 'mastodon' (CFBundleURLName org.joinmastodon.app) but no documented compose path, so do not rely on a mastodon:// prefill URL. Fallback: open https://{instance}/share?text= in Safari/SFSafariViewController.
handoff.desktop: No official desktop app. Open https://{instance}/share?text=...&url=... in the default browser (works on macOS/Windows for any Mastodon instance the user is logged into). For GoToSocial/Pixelfed use the API tier instead - no share URL.
handoff.notes: Media prefill is only via the mobile share sheet (Android ACTION_SEND/SEND_MULTIPLE with EXTRA_STREAM, iOS share extension); the web /share URL is text-only. The web route needs the right instance hostname per user - store it with the account.

text_limits.counting_rule: Grapheme clusters (Ruby String#each_grapheme_cluster.size in app/validators/status_length_validator.rb), after rewriting: every URL (with scheme) counts as exactly 23 characters (characters_reserved_per_url) regardless of length; every mention @user@domain counts as '@user' only (domain stripped); spoiler_text (content warning) is concatenated with the body and counts toward the same limit. Emoji/ZWJ sequences count as 1 each. Poll options: max 4 options x 50 graphemes (grapheme-counted), expiry 300 s .. 1 month. 500 is only the vanilla default - ALWAYS read configuration.statuses.max_characters from GET /api/v2/instance (glitch-soc/forks and GoToSocial default 5000, Mitra 5000, Pixelfed max_caption_length default 500, Pleroma/Akkoma max_toot_chars typically 5000).
text_limits.notes: No hashtag cap (hashtags count as plain characters). Pixelfed: spoiler_text max 140 and the body is strip_tags'ed; Pixelfed/GoToSocial count characters differently (PHP/Go string length, i.e. code points/bytes depending on implementation - not verified), so leave a margin on non-Mastodon servers. Pleroma/Akkoma/Mitra/GoToSocial accept content_type (text/plain, text/markdown, Akkoma also text/html, text/bbcode); Mitra DEFAULTS to text/markdown so send content_type=text/plain for literal text. 4.4+ exposes media description_limit (default 1500 on released 4.x; constant is 10,000 on main).

media_limits.image_formats: Default: image/jpeg, image/png, image/gif, image/webp (read configuration.media_attachments.supported_mime_types; HEIC/AVIF only if the instance lists them). Pixelfed default jpeg/jpg/png/gif only.
media_limits.aspect_ratio: No aspect-ratio rule; pixel-matrix limits: images <= 33,177,600 px (e.g. 7680x4320), GIF <= 921,600 px (1280x720), video <= 8,294,400 px (3840x2160) at <= 120 fps and <= 36,000 frames. Pixelfed reports image_matrix_limit 2,073,600 (1920x1080) and may re-encode (optimize_image, quality 80).
media_limits.video: 1 video (or 1 audio) per post, cannot be combined with images. Default video_size_limit 99 MiB (103,809,024 bytes); formats video/mp4, video/webm, video/quicktime, video/ogg; audio up to 99 MiB (wav/ogg/mp3/flac/aac/m4a/mp4/3gpp/webm). Video/audio uploads return 202 and must be polled. GoToSocial default media-local-max-size 40 MiB for all media, up to 6 attachments. Pixelfed video only if admin adds video/mp4 to MEDIA_TYPES; size = max_photo_size (15000 KB default).

gotchas: Confidential-client only: client_secret must be sent to /oauth/token even from mobile/desktop; since the app registers itself per instance at runtime the secret is per-user-per-instance and lives only on the device, so this is acceptable for a local-first app. Public clients (no secret) are not supported yet (PR #30329 draft, slated for 5.0).

Loopback redirect: Doorkeeper 5.9.9 ignores the port only when BOTH URIs are loopback (127.0.0.1, ::1 or localhost) and everything else (scheme, path, query) matches exactly - register http://127.0.0.1/callback (no port) and listen on an ephemeral port. Do NOT register http://localhost:0. This RFC 8252 port leniency is Doorkeeper-specific: Pixelfed (Laravel Passport), GoToSocial and Pleroma do exact matching, so for them register the exact port you will bind, or use a custom scheme / oob.

redirect_uris compatibility: Mastodon >= 4.3 accepts an array, older Mastodon, Pixelfed and Mitra expect ONE string (newline-separated for multiple). Register both 'neforum://callback' and 'http://127.0.0.1/callback' and 'urn:ietf:wg:oauth:2.0:oob' in one newline-joined string; in the oob flow the code is shown in the browser for the user to paste.
Query-string must match byte-for-byte and fragments are rejected in redirect URIs; put state in the ?state= param, not in the registered URI.

PKCE (S256 only) is optional today but will become required in Mastodon 5.0 - always send code_challenge; servers that do not support it (Pixelfed, Pleroma/Akkoma unverified, GoToSocial end-to-end unverified) simply ignore the extra params in practice, but test each.

POST /api/v1/apps is throttled to 5 per 10 minutes per IP (4.3+) - cache client_id/secret per instance on device and never re-register on each login; registering once per instance (not per account) is fine.

Scopes: request the minimum ('write:statuses write:media profile'); but Pixelfed checks tokenCan('write') (umbrella scope) for posting/uploading, and GoToSocial < 0.19.0 ignored scopes entirely, so when the server's api_versions/version indicates Pixelfed request 'read write'. verify_credentials no longer requires 'read' (4.3+): 'profile' suffices.

Idempotency-Key semantics differ: Mastodon returns the original Status (200) on replay within 1 h (handles dropped connections safely); Pixelfed returns 400 'Duplicate idempotency key.' (treat 400 after a timeout as 'probably posted'); GoToSocial ignores the header entirely (issue #2723 open) so a retry WILL double-post - dedupe locally.

Pixelfed POST /api/v1/statuses rejects posts without media unless they are replies (403 'Empty statuses are not allowed'), rejects visibility=direct (400), caps spoiler_text at 140, ignores language/scheduled_at/poll (polls config all 0), strips HTML tags, limits 1000 posts/day (429), returns 202 for every /api/v2/media upload, and /api/v1/apps returns redirect_uri (singular, comma-joined) with vapid_key null.

GoToSocial: rate limit is per client IP (300/5 min) so a shared NAT/VPN can starve you; statuses-max-chars default 5000, up to 6 attachments, 40 MiB uploads, poll hide_totals DEFAULTS TRUE; extra params local_only, content_type (text/plain|text/markdown), interaction_policy, visibility mutuals_only; scheduled_at supported (Aug 2025+, 300 total/25 per day) - older GTS (< 0.20) returns an error for scheduled_at; multipart uploads must carry a filename.

Pleroma/Akkoma: extra params content_type, preview=true (dry run, returns rendered status without posting - useful for previews), expires_in, in_reply_to_conversation_id, visibility 'local' or 'list:ID'; read limits from /api/v1/instance (max_toot_chars, upload_limit, max_media_attachments, poll_limits) because /api/v2/instance may be absent/partial; tokens may expire and refresh_token grant exists; media entities lack blurhash/meta for remote files.
Friendica: no polls (422-ish rejection), no PUT /api/v1/scheduled_statuses/:id, numeric visibility values mean circle IDs, extra friendica[title] and quote_id params.
Mitra: redirect_uris is a string, no PKCE in spec, default content_type text/markdown (send text/plain), default limit 5000, no scheduled_at.

Character counting: Mastodon counts grapheme clusters, 23 per URL, '@user' only for mentions, and the CW text counts toward the same limit; implement exactly this (use a Unicode grapheme segmenter in Dart, e.g. package 'characters') and read max_characters from /api/v2/instance per account; other servers may count code points - leave a few characters of margin when max_characters is not from Mastodon.

Media: images and video/audio cannot be mixed in one post; media OR poll, not both; a 202 upload must reach 200 on GET /api/v1/media/:id before posting or you get 422; alt text limit is description_limit (1500 on released 4.x, 5000 GoToSocial, 1000 Pixelfed).

Scheduling is server-side and limited to 300 pending / 25 per day, minimum 5 minutes ahead; the returned object is a ScheduledStatus (different shape - params.text etc.), not a Status, so the URL of the eventual post is unknown until it publishes.
Server version drift: use api_versions.mastodon (4.3+) and the 'version' string (forks embed '(compatible; Pixelfed 0.12.x)', 'GoToSocial 0.x', 'Pleroma/Akkoma ...') to switch quirk profiles.

Tokens never expire today but Mastodon plans expiry/refresh and purging tokens unused for 2 years (5.0); handle 401 by re-running the OAuth flow, and store client credentials + token with OS keychain.
Web /share hand-off needs the user logged in to that exact instance in the browser, joins title/text/url with spaces, cannot prefill media, and does not exist on GoToSocial.
Mastodon quote posts (4.5+): quoted_status_id + quote_approval_policy exist; do not send them to older servers (unknown params are ignored, but behaviour differs).
unverified_claims: Pleroma/Akkoma PKCE support: could not read their OAuth controller (GitLab/akkoma.dev served anti-bot content); recollection is that Pleroma accepts code_challenge/code_verifier but this is unverified. Their scheduled_statuses endpoints are recalled as implemented but were not re-verified.

Pixelfed uses Laravel Passport, which natively supports PKCE for public clients; whether Pixelfed's /oauth/authorize honours code_challenge for clients created via /api/v1/apps (which always get a secret) is unverified. Passport redirect matching is recalled as exact-string (no RFC 8252 loopback port leniency).

GoToSocial: its oauth2 server config allows the S256 code-challenge method, but authorize.go/token.go do not read code_challenge/code_verifier themselves; whether PKCE works end-to-end through GTS's session-based authorize flow is unverified. The exact GTS release that first shipped scheduled statuses (believed v0.20.0, after the 2025-08-12 commit) was not confirmed because Codeberg served garbage to the fetcher and the GitHub mirror tag 404'd.
Iceshrimp.NET: beyond 'Mastodon-compatible API tested against Elk/Tusky/Mona etc.' no endpoint-level details (PKCE, scheduled_at, Idempotency-Key, limits) were verified.
Tokodon reportedly switched to sending redirect_uris as a single string for compatibility (invent.kde.org MR 778) - seen only in a search-result title.
Third-party Android/iOS clients' share-intent package names and URL schemes (Tusky, Fedilab, Ivory, Ice Cubes) were not verified.

Mastodon main sets MAX_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH = 10,000 (and 4.5.8 changelog mentions raising the remote limit from 1500 to 10000); whether local uploads on released 4.4/4.5 accept more than 1500 characters is unverified - rely on description_limit.
Pixelfed and GoToSocial character-counting method (code points vs graphemes vs bytes) was not verified from source.
The 'mastodon' iOS URL scheme is recalled to support only account/status deep links, not a compose/prefill path.
Instance operators often raise MAX_CHARS via forks/patches; vanilla Mastodon hard-codes 500 (verified) and there is no env var for it in vanilla (believed true, not exhaustively checked).

web_session.how: Technically trivial but pointless: the web UI itself calls the same POST /api/v1/statuses and /api/v2/media with a session-bound bearer token that is embedded in the page's #initial-state JSON ('token'), so an embedded WebView logged into https://{instance} could inject JS to post, or simply load https://{instance}/share?text=... and let the user press Publish (login persists in the WebView's cookie jar). Recommended only as the hand-off page (WebView or system browser), never as a scraping backdoor, because the open OAuth API gives identical capabilities with no fragility.
known_libraries: None needed: use the official API (Dart: e.g. the community 'mastodon_api'/'mastodon_dart' packages or a thin http client). For a share WebView use Flutter webview_flutter / flutter_inappwebview to load https://{instance}/share.
web_session.risk: Low. No platform-wide ToS forbids automation; the API is first-class and the web client is just another API consumer. Risk is instance-specific (each server's own rules/anti-spam; Pixelfed/Mastodon antispam may silently drop posts), and WebView-based login would hide the token inside a cookie jar you cannot store securely, so it is strictly worse than OAuth.
